Proteomics analysis of human liver tissue reveals novel biomarkers for hepatocellular carcinoma.

Abstract:
We performed quantitative proteomics on liver tissue samples from patients with hepatocellular carcinoma using mass spectrometry. Human tissue samples were collected and processed for LC-MS/MS analysis on a Q Exactive HF instrument. T cells and B cells were isolated from peripheral blood for comparison.

Methods:
Samples from Homo sapiens liver tissue were digested with trypsin and analyzed using TMT labeling. Mouse liver samples were also analyzed for cross-species comparison.

Results:
We identified 5,432 proteins with high confidence. Key findings include upregulation of cancer-associated markers.
